chose: 3.9 verdict: drop 3.6, 3.7 and 3.8. Under D41's rule no thread lever goes ahead for any case. Native (3 reps, all 9/9 on the final tree) runs at 200.7k ± 61.5k tokens per task (fresh 14, cache write 11.8k, cache read 186.6k, output 2.3k), 53.6k priced, 240 ± 34 s and $0.111 per task. That beats the 3.4 serial arm (316.9k per task, +58%; priced +37%; 426 s) and the footprint-lanes arm (344.2k per task, +71%; priced +48%; 229 s). Even native's worst rep (247k) is under serial's best (294k). Across 21 agent reps there are 17 rework cases. All are merge conflicts, all are warm (gaps of 8 to 165 s), and all come from ready-scheduled lanes (2.5-lanes 9, 3.4-naive 8). Serial, footprint and default reps have 0, and no park was ever resumed. Against fresh (9.91M raw, 2.15M priced), the warm resume's lower bound comes out −19% raw and −36% priced, but its upper bound is +48% and +22%. The cold resume runs −10% priced at the lower bound and +49% at the upper. The checkpoint fork runs −28% raw and −41% priced at the lower bound, and +34% and +16% at the upper. At its best case (fork, lower bound) an arm still sits at 464k per task (2.5-lanes) or 449k (3.4-naive), 2.2× native.
over: Building threads for merge-conflict retries on the lower bound's −28% (D15, D38's expectation that thread levers close footprint lanes' +8.6%)
because: Threads only act on retries and parks, and the kept default (footprint scheduling, D37) has none. Where retries do exist, a thread wins only if it skips the retry's whole rediscovery, and even then the arm stays above native. The gap to native is per session, not per retry (results/3.9-thread-gate.json `shape`). A driven session starts at 29.6k context and makes 9.4 calls per task at a mean context of 33.2k. A native subagent starts at 15.4k and makes 4.4 calls per task at 18.2k, plus 2.5 main-thread calls per task at 47.9k. To close the gap, cut a driven session's base context and its per-task calls; resuming threads does neither. That is an operator call, outside this plan's tasks.
